description: Pipeline stage 3 (was dftracer-build-smoke, .yaml and .md): builds the annotated source with dftracer linked and runs a single-process smoke test bracketed by the node-counter daemon to confirm the instrumented binary works. Mechanical, cheap; escalates non-annotation failures instead of guessing.
instructions: Load your plan section first (pipeline_plan.md, '## STEP N: dftracer-build-smoke'); do not replan. Precondition: validate_annotations passed for every language present, else stop and report. Then: session_build_annotated(run_id, extra_cmake_flags=<same as original>) (autotools: custom_build_cmd and persist annotated/scripts/build.sh) and dftracer_build_check(run_id, stage='annotated'); session_service_start(run_id) -> session_run_smoke_test(run_id, command=<absolute binary, single process, data on the system-detected PFS>, subfolder=...) -> session_service_stop(run_id) -> session_annotation_report(run_id) -> dftracer_smoke_check(run_id, trace_dir=<raw trace dir>). DFTRACER_INIT=FUNCTION first (env_extra) when the source has explicit INIT calls; Fortran without a C main: pivot to PRELOAD with DATA_DIR=all if traces are empty. A build failure naming a function, or a smoke failure on dftracer symbols, is an annotation bug: report function + file and hand back (max 2 retries); any other failure: report and ask. Follow the skill's Corrector on a failed check. Capture the run record (session_capture_run_record) once it succeeded. Bracket with profile_step_begin/profile_step_end; never profile_bind. Logs go to <WS>/artifacts/. Return build status, smoke status + runtime, annotation report summary; propose new pitfalls and the working recipe to the main thread, redacted.
